However, it was Daizen Maeda who initially put Samurai Blue in the driving seat with a fine header two minutes before the interval, but that was cancelled out 10 minutes into the second half when Ivan Perišic equalised with a header of his own. Neither side was able to add to their tally in the rest of regulation or in extra time, and so the tie had to be settled in a penalty shootout for the first time at the Qatar tournament. Croatia's goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic demonstrated his prowess in this format as he saved the spot kicks of Takumi Minamino, Kaoru Mitoma, and Maya Yoshida and inspired his nation to a 3-1 triumph

programme.desc: Coverage of the seventh round-of-16 match (Kick-off 5.00pm), which takes place at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. The fans in attendance will hope for a more entertaining affair than in the corresponding clash in Al Rayyan four years ago, as Morocco and Spain played out a monotonous 0-0 draw over 120 minutes, in which the Spanish dominated possession but did little with it as few chances were created. The tie came to life in the subsequent penalty shootout as the 2010 champions failed to convert any of their three attempts with goalkeeper Yassine Bounou saving from Sergio Busquets and Carlos Soler after Pablo Sarabia first hit the post, while the Atlas Lions scored three of their four penalties to progress. By missing their three spot kicks, Spain became only the second team to not score in a World Cup penalty shoot-out, following in the footsteps of Switzerland who lost to Ukraine in 2006 by the same 3-0 scoreline

programme.desc: Coverage of the eighth round-of-16 match (Kick-off 9.00pm), which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. The concluding match of this stage four years ago proved to be memorable for several reasons, not the least the final score, as Portugal claimed a comprehensive 6-1 victory over Switzerland. This despite the fact Cristiano Ronaldo was left out of the starting line-up for the first time in a major tournament since Euro 2008 with Gonçalo Ramos making his first start instead, which proved to be a wise move as Ramos became the youngest to score a World Cup hat-trick since Flórián Albert in 1962. Others to get their name on the scoresheet were Raphaël Guerreiro, Rafael Leão, and experienced centre-back Pepe, who became the oldest player to score in the World Cup knockout stage and the second oldest to score at any stage, behind Cameroon's Roger Milla

However, it was Daizen Maeda who initially put Samurai Blue in the driving seat with a fine header two minutes before the interval, but that was cancelled out 10 minutes into the second half when Ivan Perišic equalised with a header of his own. Neither side was able to add to their tally in the rest of regulation or in extra time, and so the tie had to be settled in a penalty shootout for the first time at the Qatar tournament. Croatia's goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic demonstrated his prowess in this format as he saved the spot kicks of Takumi Minamino, Kaoru Mitoma, and Maya Yoshida and inspired his nation to a 3-1 triumph

The fans in attendance will hope for a more entertaining affair than in the corresponding clash in Al Rayyan four years ago, as Morocco and Spain played out a monotonous 0-0 draw over 120 minutes, in which the Spanish dominated possession but did little with it as few chances were created. The tie came to life in the subsequent penalty shootout as the 2010 champions failed to convert any of their three attempts with goalkeeper Yassine Bounou saving from Sergio Busquets and Carlos Soler after Pablo Sarabia first hit the post, while the Atlas Lions scored three of their four penalties to progress. By missing their three spot kicks, Spain became only the second team to not score in a World Cup penalty shoot-out, following in the footsteps of Switzerland who lost to Ukraine in 2006 by the same 3-0 scoreline

However, it was Daizen Maeda who initially put Samurai Blue in the driving seat with a fine header two minutes before the interval, but that was cancelled out 10 minutes into the second half when Ivan Perišic equalised with a header of his own. Neither side was able to add to their tally in the rest of regulation or in extra time, and so the tie had to be settled in a penalty shootout for the first time at the Qatar tournament. The deadlock lasted just seven minutes as Vinícius Júnior opened the scoring with a neat side-foot finish that three Korean defenders positioned on the line could not block, and the lead was doubled six minutes later when Neymar scored from the penalty spot. programme.desc: Coverage of the seventh round-of-16 match (Kick-off 5.00pm), which takes place at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. The fans in attendance will hope for a more entertaining affair than in the corresponding clash in Al Rayyan four years ago, as Morocco and Spain played out a monotonous 0-0 draw over 120 minutes, in which the Spanish dominated possession but did little with it as few chances were created. The tie came to life in the subsequent penalty shootout as the 2010 champions failed to convert any of their three attempts with goalkeeper Yassine Bounou saving from Sergio Busquets and Carlos Soler after Pablo Sarabia first hit the post, while the Atlas Lions scored three of their four penalties to progress. By missing their three spot kicks, Spain became only the second team to not score in a World Cup penalty shoot-out, following in the footsteps of Switzerland who lost to Ukraine in 2006 by the same 3-0 scoreline

This despite the fact Cristiano Ronaldo was left out of the starting line-up for the first time in a major tournament since Euro 2008 with Gonçalo Ramos making his first start instead, which proved to be a wise move as Ramos became the youngest to score a World Cup hat-trick since Flórián Albert in 1962. programme.desc: Coverage of the fifth round-of-16 match (Kick-off 8.00pm), which takes place at Dallas Stadium in the USA. 2018 runners-up Croatia battled past a defiant Japan at this stage four year ago, eventually overcoming them on penalties to secure a place in the last eight. However, it was Daizen Maeda who initially put Samurai Blue in the driving seat with a fine header two minutes before the interval, but that was cancelled out 10 minutes into the second half when Ivan Perišic equalised with a header of his own. Neither side was able to add to their tally in the rest of regulation or in extra time, and so the tie had to be settled in a penalty shootout for the first time at the Qatar tournament. Croatia's goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic demonstrated his prowess in this format as he saved the spot kicks of Takumi Minamino, Kaoru Mitoma, and Maya Yoshida and inspired his nation to a 3-1 triumph

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Coverage of the sixth round-of-16 match (Kick-off 1.00am), which takes place at Seattle Stadium in the USA. Four different scorers got their names on the scoresheet in a 4-1 win for Brazil over South Korea in the corresponding fixture four years ago, as the five-time champions easily advanced to the quarter-finals. The deadlock lasted just seven minutes as Vinícius Júnior opened the scoring with a neat side-foot finish that three Korean defenders positioned on the line could not block, and the lead was doubled six minutes later when Neymar scored from the penalty spot. The Seleção continued their dominance as Richarlison and Lucas Paquetá ensured they went into the half-time interval four goals to the good, and despite a spectacular thirty-yard strike from Paik Seung-ho in the second-half, it proved to be no more than a consolation

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Coverage of the seventh round-of-16 match (Kick-off 5.00pm), which takes place at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. The fans in attendance will hope for a more entertaining affair than in the corresponding clash in Al Rayyan four years ago, as Morocco and Spain played out a monotonous 0-0 draw over 120 minutes, in which the Spanish dominated possession but did little with it as few chances were created. The tie came to life in the subsequent penalty shootout as the 2010 champions failed to convert any of their three attempts with goalkeeper Yassine Bounou saving from Sergio Busquets and Carlos Soler after Pablo Sarabia first hit the post, while the Atlas Lions scored three of their four penalties to progress. By missing their three spot kicks, Spain became only the second team to not score in a World Cup penalty shoot-out, following in the footsteps of Switzerland who lost to Ukraine in 2006 by the same 3-0 scoreline

programme.desc: Coverage of the eighth round-of-16 match (Kick-off 9.00pm), which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. The concluding match of this stage four years ago proved to be memorable for several reasons, not the least the final score, as Portugal claimed a comprehensive 6-1 victory over Switzerland. This despite the fact Cristiano Ronaldo was left out of the starting line-up for the first time in a major tournament since Euro 2008 with Gonçalo Ramos making his first start instead, which proved to be a wise move as Ramos became the youngest to score a World Cup hat-trick since Flórián Albert in 1962. Others to get their name on the scoresheet were Raphaël Guerreiro, Rafael Leão, and experienced centre-back Pepe, who became the oldest player to score in the World Cup knockout stage and the second oldest to score at any stage, behind Cameroon's Roger Milla
